selectionReason: Five substantive milestones spanning early form, injury, roster reinforcement and postseason advancement. Sasaki signing rejected because it predates exact contract creation. Selected without viewing price history.

cards.title: Ohtani walks it off; Dodgers start 8–0
cards.fact: Los Angeles remains unbeaten after defeating Atlanta 6–5.
cards.rationale: Early dominance offers evidence for the defending champion’s strength, though eight games is a small sample.

cards.title: Sasaki stops throwing, with no return timeline
cards.fact: Shoulder discomfort interrupts the rookie pitcher’s rehabilitation.
cards.rationale: Losing rotation depth could weaken the title bid; other returning pitchers and team results also matter.

cards.title: Dodgers acquire reliever Brock Stewart at the deadline
cards.fact: Los Angeles sends James Outman to Minnesota in the trade.
cards.rationale: Bullpen reinforcement can matter in October, but one reliever may barely alter championship expectations. Other deadline deals share this window.

cards.title: Dodgers clinch the NL West
cards.fact: Los Angeles wins its fourth consecutive division title.
cards.rationale: Winning the division clarifies the postseason route, though qualification and the division result may already be expected.

cards.title: Dodgers sweep Milwaukee to reach the World Series
cards.fact: Ohtani hits three home runs in the clincher.
cards.rationale: Only the championship series remains; this is advancement toward the contract outcome, not the resolving victory.
